text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded. Every number matches the card: 17.3% of 579 claims vs 4.1% expected, z 2.43, 24% low-complexity share, 30 documented claims, 4 of 5 99215 below billed (80%) vs 6.7%, and 1 of 20 with no lab line. The 7 of 24 headline figure is correct: 99214 has 3 below billed and 99215 has 4, giving 7 of 24 documented. The language is cautious (\"reason to review, not a finding\"), the next steps are concrete, and the cited claims fit their sentences. Weaknesses remain. The example claims are partly weak, and C0017188 is described as heart failure with 1 condition, which is clinically significant but listed as low complexity. The summary does not state explicitly that the sample of 5 documented 99215s is small. It never mentions the one 99215 that was supported (C0017052) or that complexity-stratified shares are high even for patients with 3-4 conditions. The \"7% comparison\" is correct but the card gives 0.067, so rounding is fine. The headline combines 99214 and 99215, while the rationale emphasizes 99215 only. The \"copied forward\" step is generic.","problems":["Small sample (5 documented 99215 claims) is not flagged as a limitation","Does not mention the documented 99215 that was supported (C0017052), so the picture is one-sided","Headline mixes 99214 and 99215, while the rationale focuses on 99215 alone, which is slightly inconsistent","Three of the six cited claims have no documentation outcome, only low-complexity details, so the evidence for them is thin","Last next step (copied-forward notes) is generic and not tied to any evidence in the packet","Does not note that the patients' underlying conditions may not reflect visit-level complexity"]}
